source: English.pdf — MIE Teaching and Learning Syllabus, English, Grades 1 to 6, the 'NCF GRAMMAR SYLLABUS' table, Grade 6 column (printed pages 19-22)
note: One entry per item the Grade 6 column of the grammar table names. `any` = covered when some question's stem or answer contains ANY of these phrases. `all` = covered only when ONE question contains ALL of them. Terms are matched against the question STEM AND ANSWER ONLY, never the explanation: a fact mentioned in an explanation is a fact the child is never asked. ⚠ SCOPE: the grammar table only. The rest of this syllabus is four competency matrices (listening, speaking, reading, writing) whose rows are skills — 'show willingness to engage in writing activities' — and whose grade is marked by SHADING, not text. A skill of that kind cannot be detected by matching words in a question stem, and nothing here should be read as saying those competencies are covered or uncovered. The grammar table is different: it names the items, in text, in a column headed Grade 6, and it is what the PSAC paper's grammar questions test. ⚠ Phonics at Grade 6 is 'reinforce according to learners' needs' and names no item, so it carries no entry.

facts.fact: Frequently used abstract nouns (pollution, happiness, friendship)
Form a noun from an adjective (happy - happiness)
Form a noun from a verb (pollute - pollution)
Form adjectives from nouns or verbs (shine - shiny, metal - metallic, wood - wooden)
Use of adverbs to modify adjectives (very slow, too good)
Words taking no article (I went to school)
Quantifiers: both, all, enough, less, more
Complex sentences formed with relative pronouns
The relative pronouns who, which, that, whose, where, when, why
Conjunctions of reason: because, as, for
Conjunctions of cause and effect: so that, therefore
